installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Battlefront Eternal dedicated server (bfeserver)
#
# Server files: /mnt/server
#   bfe/        the newest release's server, engine and preparation tools
#   bfe-data/   game data, prepared from the owned game by those tools
#   bfe-state/  config.json, the server's identity and its player statistics
#   game/       the owned game: the folder that holds GameData

cd /mnt/server || exit 1
mkdir -p bfe-state game

if [ "$(uname -m)" = "aarch64" ]; then ARCH=arm64; else ARCH=amd64; fi

## The owned game, STAR WARS Battlefront (Classic, 2004), from Steam when an account is set
if [ -n "${STEAM_USER}" ] && [ "${ARCH}" != "amd64" ]; then
    echo "SteamCMD needs an x86_64 node. Upload the game's GameData folder to game/ instead."
elif [ -n "${STEAM_USER}" ]; then
    mkdir -p steamcmd
    curl -fsSL https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar -xz -C steamcmd || exit 1
    # SteamCMD keeps its login in /mnt/server/Steam, so a Steam Guard code is only needed once.
    chown -R root:root /mnt/server
    export HOME=/mnt/server
    ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows +force_install_dir /mnt/server/game +login "${STEAM_USER}" "${STEAM_PASS}" ${STEAM_AUTH} +app_update 1058020 validate +quit
fi

## Battlefront Eternal: the server, engine and preparation tools of the newest release
FEED=https://get.battlefronteternal.com/downloads/latest
SUMS=$(curl -fsSL "${FEED}/SHA256SUMS") || { echo "Could not reach ${FEED}"; exit 1; }
DEB=$(echo "${SUMS}" | grep -o "battlefront-eternal_[^ ]*_${ARCH}\.deb" | head -n 1)
[ -n "${DEB}" ] || { echo "No ${ARCH} release in ${FEED}"; exit 1; }
echo "Downloading Battlefront Eternal $(echo "${DEB}" | cut -d _ -f 2)"
# The package is bigger than the installer's /tmp, so it is downloaded here and removed after.
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "${DEB}" "${FEED}/${DEB}" && echo "${SUMS}" | grep " ${DEB}$" | sha256sum -c - || { rm -f "${DEB}"; exit 1; }
rm -rf bfe && mkdir bfe
dpkg-deb --fsys-tarfile "${DEB}" | tar -x -C bfe --strip-components=4 \
    "./opt/Battlefront Eternal/resources/host-runtime" "./opt/Battlefront Eternal/resources/tools" \
    "./opt/Battlefront Eternal/resources/toolchain" "./opt/Battlefront Eternal/resources/bfe-tree.json" || { rm -f "${DEB}"; exit 1; }
rm -f "${DEB}"

## Server configuration, kept on reinstall
if [ ! -f bfe-state/config.json ]; then
    cat > bfe-state/config.json << 'EOF'
{
  "name": "Battlefront Eternal server",
  "gamePort": 18451,
  "maxPlayers": 64,
  "rotation": [
    "swbf1/nab2:rep:conquest",
    "swbf1/hot1:imp:conquest",
    "swbf1/kas2:rep:conquest",
    "swbf1/tat2:imp:conquest",
    "swbf1/bes2:rep:conquest",
    "swbf1/end1:imp:conquest"
  ],
  "discovery": false,
  "onlineNoticeAccepted": false,
  "relayPolicy": "auto",
  "honorGlobalBans": true
}
EOF
fi

## Game data, prepared again only when the release's tools or their Python change
KEY=$(jq -r '.files[] | select((.path | startswith("resources/tools/")) or (.path | startswith("resources/toolchain/python/"))) | "\(.path) \(.sha256)"' bfe/bfe-tree.json | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum | cut -c 1-32)
GAMEDATA=$(find /mnt/server/game -maxdepth 2 -type d -name GameData -print -quit)
if [ "$(cat bfe-data/.bfe-data-key 2>/dev/null)" = "${KEY}" ]; then
    echo "The prepared game data is current"
elif [ -z "${GAMEDATA}" ] && [ -n "${STEAM_USER}" ]; then
    echo "SteamCMD did not install the game. Check the Steam username, password and Steam Guard code, then reinstall the server."
elif [ -z "${GAMEDATA}" ]; then
    echo "No game found. Set a Steam account that owns STAR WARS Battlefront (Classic, 2004),"
    echo "or upload the game's GameData folder to game/, then reinstall the server."
else
    # One job takes up to 1.5 GB of memory and each further job up to 0.5 GB more.
    JOBS=$(nproc)
    MEMORY=$(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes 2>/dev/null | grep -m 1 -x '[0-9]*')
    MEMORY=$(( ${MEMORY:-0} / 1048576 ))
    if [ "${MEMORY}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${MEMORY}" -lt 1536 ]; then
        echo "Preparing the game data needs 1.5 GB of memory, and the installer has ${MEMORY} MB. Give the server more memory, then reinstall it."
        exit 1
    elif [ "${MEMORY}" -gt 0 ] && [ $(( 1 + (MEMORY - 1536) / 512 )) -lt "${JOBS}" ]; then
        JOBS=$(( 1 + (MEMORY - 1536) / 512 ))
    fi
    echo "Preparing the game data, ${JOBS} job(s) at a time. This takes a few minutes."
    rm -rf bfe-data.new bfe-tmp && mkdir bfe-data.new bfe-tmp
    # prepare.py exits 0 when only a map or an army failed, so its record is checked too.
    if ! (cd bfe/tools && env -i PATH=/mnt/server/bfe/toolchain/bin:/usr/bin:/bin HOME=/mnt/server/bfe-tmp TMPDIR=/mnt/server/bfe-tmp LANG=C.UTF-8 \
        BFE_GAME_DIR="$(dirname "${GAMEDATA}")" BFE_CONTENT_DIR=/mnt/server/bfe-data.new KTX2_ENCODER=off \
        PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 \
        ../toolchain/python/bin/python3 -u prepare.py --core-only --jobs "${JOBS}") \
        || [ "$(jq '.failed | length' bfe-data.new/.prepare.json 2>/dev/null)" != 0 ]; then
        jq -r '.failures[]? | "\(.label): \(.reason)"' bfe-data.new/.prepare.json 2>/dev/null
        rm -rf bfe-data.new bfe-tmp
        echo "Preparing the game data failed. Check the game files, or give the server more memory, then reinstall it."
        exit 1
    fi
    echo "${KEY}" > bfe-data.new/.bfe-data-key
    rm -rf bfe-data bfe-tmp && mv bfe-data.new bfe-data
fi

echo "Battlefront Eternal installed"

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name players see in the server browser and when they join.

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: How many people can join, up to 64 (32 a side). Bots fill the rest of each army.

variables.name: Steam Username
variables.description: A Steam account that owns STAR WARS Battlefront (Classic, 2004), to download the game during installation. Leave empty to upload the game's GameData folder to game/ yourself (a Steam or GOG copy).

variables.name: Steam Password
variables.description: The Steam account's password. Only the installation uses it.

variables.name: Steam Guard Code
variables.description: A current Steam Guard code, if the account asks for one. SteamCMD remembers the login after it succeeds.
